q: The mass of an object is a measure of the ____ in it.
e: The mass of an object is a measure of the amount of matter in it. Amount of matter here means anything that has mass and occupies space.

q: Mass is measured in laboratories using a sliding mass balance or the ____.
e: Mass is measured in laboratories using a sliding mass balance or the electronic balance. The physics in this sentence is built around electronic balance.

q: The electronic balance is easier to use and also ____ than sliding mass balance.
e: The electronic balance is easier to use and also more accurate than sliding mass balance. The physics in this sentence is built around more accurate.

q: The unknown mass is placed on the top of the pan and its mass is read directly from a ____.
e: The unknown mass is placed on the top of the pan and its mass is read directly from a display screen. The physics in this sentence is built around display screen.

q: The balance really detects the gravitational pull on the object (____), but the scale is marked to show the mass.
e: The balance really detects the gravitational pull on the object (weight), but the scale is marked to show the mass. Weight here means the gravitational pull of the Earth on a body, a downward force. Weight is mg, a force toward Earth's centre, not the same as mass.

q: The mass of purified drinking water of 1 litre bottle is ____.
e: The mass of purified drinking water of 1 litre bottle is 1 kg. The physics in this sentence is built around 1 kg.
